label: v186
changes: Teluva can now read scanned documents. Most of what a family actually keeps is a photo or a scan — a lease off the copier, an insurance letter photographed on the kitchen table — and until now Teluva could only read documents that were born as digital text. Ask about a scanned lease and you now get the clause back, quoted, with its page number.

It tells you when it read from a picture rather than from text. Passages from a scan carry a "read from an image" tag, because reading ink off a photograph is a different kind of certainty to reading a text file — and Teluva still will not tell you your document doesn't say something, since a word it misread looks exactly like a word that was never there.
A page it couldn't make out is named, not skipped. If three pages of a nine-page scan are too blurred to read, it says which three rather than quietly searching the other six and calling it done.
Reading a scan happens once. The result is kept with the document, so every question after the first comes back straight away.
